Maya (CS): Heads-up 10 -- Helios Bio procurement asked for a concise SLA one-pager to include in their contract packet. They want: uptime metric name, latency targets (p50/p95), credit calc + cap, and a short onboarding schedule. Renewal check-in ~5 weeks. Can @Diego and @Rhea confirm wording and numbers?
Diego (SRE): short: hosted API SLO = 99.9% monthly uptime (we call it MUP). p50 target = 120ms, p95 = 350ms on standard inference endpoints. Dedicated commitments: 99.95% MUP, expect p95 ~400-700ms during initial model warm-up windows.
Rhea (Solutions): agree. Add note: "Latency SLOs measured during steady-state traffic; first 60-90 minutes after model rollouts or large scale events may exceed targets due to KV cache and JIT compilation."
Maya (CS): credits: do we have a customer-friendly formula + a worked example? Keep it simple for procurement.
Diego (SRE): use this friendly snippet customers understand: ```credit = min(0.25, (SLO_target - observed_MUP) / SLO_target) * committed_monthly_fee``` cap = 25% monthly. Example: committed $8,000/mo, target 99.9%, observed 99.5% -> shortfall = 0.4% -> credit = min(25%, 0.004/0.999) * $8,000 ~ $32.
Rhea (Solutions): I'll make a tiny table: rows for Hosted vs Dedicated, show SLO, typical p95, credit cap, lead time for Dedicated (2-3 weeks), and recommended add-ons (reserved pool, pre-warm slot, burst-protection).
Sanjay (AE): Helios is worried about short bursts during batch ingest. Recommend we offer a pre-warm window (1 hour) + reserved concurrency as an add-on on the renewal. I'll draft pricing bullets.
Maya (CS): FYI procurement also asked for an evidence link showing how we compute MUP. Diego can we paste a monitoring query or a dashboard link?
Diego (SRE): yes. Metric name = "monthly uptime percentage (MUP)". Example PromQL to compute hourly-aggregated MUP over 30d: `sum_over_time(up{service="inference-api"}[30d]) / (30*24*3600)` We'll publish a dashboard snapshot link once Rhea finalizes wording.
Rhea (Solutions): onboarding flow (short): Day 0: kickoff + credentials exchange; Day 1: integration tests + small-scale traffic; Day 3: performance tuning + canary; Day 7: scale to steady-state. Call this "Typical 1-week ramp" with optional accelerated path (3-4 days) if we preschedule a dedicated warm-up slot.
Maya (CS): action items: (1) Diego - paste final dashboard link & monitoring query; (2) Rhea - produce one-pager + simple table and attach as PDF; (3) Sanjay - write add-on bullets and preliminary pricing; (4) I'll send to Helios procurement by Friday EOD.
ProcBot: Reminder created: send follow-up to thread at 2024-03-22T16:00:00Z.
Diego (SRE): small legal note: multi-region customers get per-region SLOs; aggregate reported availability on customer reports but SLA credits apply per-region unless otherwise negotiated. I'll add a short sentence.
Rhea (Solutions): adding a plain-language line about warm-up and pinned model versions. Also including the worked example table and a one-sentence FAQ: "How credits are issued: credits are applied to next invoice; they are not cash refunds."
Maya (CS): perfect. Please drop your final snippets into this doc: https://redwood.docs/helios/sla-onepager-draft by Thursday 10:00 PT so I can finalize. :rocket:
